hints: For a k by k board, count all unordered pairs of distinct squares first.
Each pair is attacked only if the knights occupy one of the 2-by-3 rectangles in a possible orientation.
There are 4(k-1)(k-2) attacking pairs; subtract them from the total pairs.
analogy: Start with every possible pair of squares, then remove the pairs where the two knights can jump at each other.
example: On a 3 by 3 board there are choose(9,2)=36 pairs and 4(2)(1)=8 attacking pairs, leaving 28.
algorithm: For each k from 1 to n, compute k^2(k^2-1)/2 - 4(k-1)(k-2), treating the second term as zero when k<3.
correctness: Every placement is one unordered pair; the rectangle count enumerates every attacking knight pair exactly once, so the subtraction leaves precisely safe placements.
complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space beyond the n outputs; use a wide integer type.
